newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's o/n rates end down on liquid mkt.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's o/n rates end down on liquid mkt.

text.p: Hungary's overnight rates continued to ease on Tuesday on abundant market liquidity, boosted by money from matured one-month reverse repo deals, traders said.
"An abundance of funds was felt on the forint market," said Sandor Tolonics of Commerzbank.
The overnight rates moved around 20.00 percent on Tuesday and closed at 19.875 percent, down from Monday's closing of 20.25 percent.
The overnight rates have been dropping from 20.75 percent levels since Friday following a rise probably fuelled by customer orders of some large banks.
Traders said that market liquidity was improved partly by interest payments on Friday to banks on government bonds issued in Hungary's banking consolidation programme.
Substantial money was likely to have flowed back onto the market from matured one-month reverse repo deals, placed there before repo rate cuts in the middle of June, traders added.
They said that the overnight rates were likely to stay around 20 percent until the end of the two-week reserve period at the end of the month.
